title: U.S. House · Kansas's 3rd District
area: Northeast Kansas, mainly Wyandotte and Johnson Counties (Kansas City, KS and its suburbs)

context.text: Incumbent Sharice Davids (D) defeated primary challenger Sarah Preu, 83.4% to 16.6%, in her first contested primary since being elected in 2018. Eric Jenkins, a retired Army colonel and former Shawnee City Council member, defeated Chase LaPorte in the Republican primary after filing near the June 1 deadline. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is D+2, the most competitive of Kansas's four districts.

summary.text: Sharice Davids is the Democratic incumbent representing Kansas's 3rd District, first elected in 2018 and in office since January 2019. A member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, she is a Cornell-trained lawyer who worked in economic development on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, was a White House Fellow, and competed professionally in mixed martial arts before entering politics. She is seeking a fifth term.

background.text: According to her official House biography, she was raised by a single mother who served in the Army for 20 years, graduated from Leavenworth High School, and was a first-generation college student who worked throughout college.

Earned an associate degree from Johnson County Community College (2003), a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Missouri-Kansas City (2007), and a law degree from Cornell Law School (2010).

Worked as an associate at SNR Denton and as of-counsel at Ceiba Legal, as chair of the board of Twelve Clans, Inc. for the Ho-Chunk Nation, as deputy director of the Thunder Valley Community Development Corporation on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, and as director of economic development at Red Cloud Indian School.
Served as a White House Fellow in the Department of Transportation under President Barack Obama.
Is a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation and competed in professional mixed martial arts (1-1 record).
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018, succeeding Kevin Yoder, and took office January 3, 2019; she and Deb Haaland of New Mexico were among the first two Native American women elected to Congress.
In the 2025-2026 Congress she serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.
Her official biography lists her residence as Roeland Park.

priorities.text: Filed for a fifth term casting herself as a check on what she called "extremism" in Washington, D.C.
Lowering health care and prescription drug costs, strengthening the Affordable Care Act, and expanding Medicaid.
Shifting to renewable energy and clean-energy manufacturing while protecting public lands and waters.
Protecting voting rights, defending access to reproductive health care, and keeping communities safe.

positions.summary: Says she is working to strengthen the Affordable Care Act and expand Medicaid, and highlights voting to let Medicare negotiate lower prescription drug prices.
positions.quote: That’s why I’m dedicated to finding ways to lower the cost of health care and prescription drugs, strengthen the Affordable Care Act, expand Medicaid, and improve quality of care.

positions.summary: Supports shifting to renewable energy and cites her vote for the Inflation Reduction Act's climate investments, which she says puts the U.S. on a path to cut greenhouse gas emissions.
positions.quote: I believe we should create a world and an economy our grandchildren can thrive in.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to ensure access to the full range of health care services, including reproductive health care, without political interference.
positions.quote: Health care decisions should be between you and your doctor – without the interference of politicians. I will always fight to ensure Kansas families have access to the full range of health care services they need, including reproductive health care.

positions.summary: Says she voted to pass gun violence prevention legislation to protect children and keep schools safe.
positions.quote: I also voted to pass historic, bipartisan gun violence prevention legislation to protect Kansas children and keep our schools safe.

positions.summary: Says she secured federal funding for local police units, including a new Mobile Command Unit for the Olathe Police Department.
positions.quote: I secured federal funding for local police units, including helping purchase a new Mobile Command Unit at the Olathe Police Department.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit) and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit), 2025-2026 assignments.

candidates.name: Eric Jenkins
candidates.currentRole: Former Shawnee City Council member (two terms, Ward 2)

summary.text: Eric Jenkins is a retired U.S. Army colonel and former Shawnee, Kansas city councilmember who won the Republican nomination for Kansas's 3rd District. He spent decades with the Federal Emergency Management Agency and in Shawnee city government, and according to his campaign website is running on fiscal responsibility, lower taxes, and border security and national defense.

background.text: Retired as a colonel in the U.S. Army.
Spent 30 years with the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
Spent 28 years in Shawnee, Kansas city government, including on the Shawnee Planning Commission and two terms on the city council representing Ward 2.
Lost his 2023 city council reelection bid to Jeanie Murphy.
Announced his congressional campaign on May 28, 2026, shortly before Kansas's June 1 filing deadline, and advanced from the August 4 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Campaign platform focuses on fiscal responsibility, lowering taxes for families and Kansas businesses, and strong border security and national defense.

Says he is running to fight for safer communities, lower costs, secure borders, and accountable government, and criticizes Davids for backing Biden-era policy and opposing Trump administration border and public-safety efforts.
priorities.quote: Sharice Davids spent years backing the Biden-Harris agenda that drove up costs, weakened our economy, and failed to secure the border.

positions.summary: Campaigns on strong border security and supports the Trump administration's border enforcement efforts.

candidates.researchNotes: Jenkins has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from a Johnson County Post news report citing his campaign announcement and website.

candidates.name: Steve Hohe

summary.text: Steve Hohe is a retired U.S. Air Force veteran and former businessman running as the Libertarian Party candidate. He has previously run as a Libertarian for the U.S. House in 2020 and 2022 and for the Kansas House in 2024.

background.text: Lived in Kansas City, Missouri before joining the U.S. Air Force, where he served from 1980 to 1991, mainly in the Strategic Air Command and during Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm, according to his Ballotpedia survey response.
Earned an associate degree from the Community College of the Air Force (1991) and a bachelor's degree from Husson College (1992).
Moved to Kansas after leaving the Air Force and, in his own words, lived in Shawnee for over 25 years; describes himself as a former owner of two businesses, married with two children.
Was a candidate in the general elections for Kansas's 3rd Congressional District in 2020 and 2022, both won by Sharice Davids, and for Kansas House District 18 in 2024, won by Cindy Neighbor.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements on policy issues found; background is limited to Ballotpedia's biographical summary. He has not completed the Candidate Connection survey.
